task.title: R1B follow-up B: same-key re-entrancy into runExclusive self-deadlocks silently with no guard
task.objective: src/storage/folderWriteCoordinator.ts serializes every mutation for a resolved folder onto one lane by chaining owned.tail.then(task, task). A task already running on a lane that calls runExclusive again for the SAME key therefore awaits a tail that only settles once that task itself returns, so it deadlocks permanently with no timeout and no diagnostic: pending never reaches zero, the lane is never evicted, and because lanes are keyed by folder and shared process-wide, every store in the Electron main process pointed at that folder wedges silently for the life of the process. The verifiers have no per-check timeout, so the symptom is a CI job timeout with no failing assertion name, which is a strictly worse signal than a red. The shipped code is CORRECT - ProfileStore.ts:190-196 documents the hazard and both composite operations call the unlocked internals - so this task does not fix a live defect; it converts a silent permanent hang into an immediate diagnosable rejection if that discipline is ever broken. KNOWN_ISSUES records two remedy options: a source-level lexical guard, or a runtime same-key re-entrancy throw in runExclusive. Take the runtime option, because it rejects at the moment the re-entrancy occurs rather than only where it is lexically visible.

architecture: The guard belongs in runExclusive in src/storage/folderWriteCoordinator.ts and nowhere else. Do not add a guard to JsonProfileStore.serialize, do not change ProfileStore's public interface, and do not alter writeProfileUnlocked or deleteUnlocked.

A synchronous re-entrancy flag cannot work and must not be used. Rejecting every new same-key arrival while a task is running would reject LEGITIMATE external callers queued from outside, which is the coordinator's entire purpose. Only async context distinguishes 'queued from outside the running task' from 'called from inside it', so node:async_hooks AsyncLocalStorage is required.

node:async_hooks is a Node core module, not a package dependency. package.json dependencies, devDependencies and every other manifest field are unchanged, so this is not a new_dependency and no Release handoff is implied. This is the first AsyncLocalStorage usage in src/, which is why the reasoning is recorded here rather than assumed.
Detect BEFORE mutating any lane state. A rejected re-entrant call must leave owned.pending and the lanes map exactly as it found them, or the guard would itself strand the lane it exists to protect.
Return a rejected promise rather than throwing synchronously, so runExclusive's promise-returning contract is unchanged for every caller.

Scope is same-key re-entrancy only. Cross-key cycles - task on folder A calling runExclusive on folder B which is itself waiting on A - are a different hazard and are explicitly out of scope; do not attempt a general cycle detector.
security: No authorization, licensing, secret-handling or protected-login surface is touched. No IPC channel, permission or sender check changes.
compatibility: Every currently legitimate call must behave exactly as before: FIFO ordering, one-at-a-time per resolved folder, a failed task rejecting for its own caller without blocking those queued behind it, and lane eviction when pending reaches zero. The only new behavior is a rejection on a call that would previously have hung forever.
No persisted shape change, no migration, no JSON round-trip change. folderCoordinationKey and activeFolderCoordinationKeys keep their exact signatures and semantics.

Preserve offline operation, the bundled Chromium, and the no-global-Node / no-global-Playwright / no-admin constraints. No new npm script - verify:write-queue and verify:profile-store are already registered in scripts/lib/verifier-classification.ts.
offline: No network access, no new package dependency, no packaging change.
exclusions: Do NOT fix the separately tracked open finding at docs/ai/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:288-291 - that the coordinator's comments attribute the non-poisoning guarantee to the unreachable rejected arm of then(task, task) rather than to the settled assignment. It is a comment-accuracy defect in the same file and is deliberately left alone.

Do NOT address awkit-s410 (QC finding A, vacuous lane-eviction evidence), awkit-9a1l (R2 follow-up A), QC finding C (path aliasing splitting a lane), the whole-document last-admitted-writer-wins update semantics, the in-process-only boundary, or gateBoundDominatesAFreeWriter at docs/ai/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:283-287.
Do NOT reopen or re-run completed awkit-ttvb, awkit-syaa, SEC-005 or the UI migration.

acceptance.description: runExclusive rejects, rather than hanging, when it is called for a key that is already held by the task currently executing on that key's lane. The rejection is a real Error carrying the coordination key and naming the hazard, so a future violator gets a diagnosable red instead of a CI timeout with no assertion name.

A task running on folder A may still call runExclusive for a DIFFERENT folder B and have it run normally. The guard keys on the coordination key, not on 'am I inside any task', so legitimate nesting across folders is unaffected. This assertion is proven non-vacuous by its own mutant.

A rejected re-entrant call leaves the lane exactly as it found it: pending is not incremented, owned.tail is not reassigned, and the lane is still evicted normally once the outer task settles. Measured through activeFolderCoordinationKeys, with a cardinality assertion before any emptiness assertion so the check cannot pass over an empty set.

The new check was executed against the UNGUARDED coordinator first and observed FAIL, before any edit to src/storage/folderWriteCoordinator.ts. Because removing the guard makes a naive re-entrancy test HANG rather than fail - the exact worse-than-red symptom this task exists to eliminate - the check itself races the re-entrant call against a bounded timeout and asserts that it settled as a rejection carrying the guard's error. A timeout is recorded as a FAIL with a named assertion, never as a hang. No existing assertion was weakened to produce green.

Each independently load-bearing assertion is proven to reject a broken source shape, with the observed failing assertion read from output rather than predicted: deleting the guard, making its condition always false, and widening it to reject ANY nested call regardless of key - the third being what proves the different-keys assertion is not vacuous. A TypeScript compile error is never accepted as mutation evidence. Source is restored byte-exactly after each mutant and no mutation remains on disk, confirmed by git status against src/storage/folderWriteCoordinator.ts.

No currently legitimate caller changes behavior. npm run build typechecks clean, verify:write-queue and verify:profile-store keep every pre-existing assertion passing at or above their measured baseline counts, and verify:r0-characterization - which holds the R1B coordination characterizations - is unchanged at its recorded total. Deltas are attributed to the specific checks added, not asserted as unchanged when they moved.

The implementation diff touches src/storage/folderWriteCoordinator.ts and scripts/verify-write-queue.mts only. src/storage/ProfileStore.ts is unmodified, no other src/storage module is altered, no new verifier script or npm script is created, and every exclusion listed in constraints.exclusions is left alone. No protected owner path is staged.

The mock-site applicability rule is answered from mock-site/README.md rather than assumed, and the answer is recorded with its exact reason. This evidence item is an applicability DETERMINATION: PASS attests that the determination was executed and returned a definitive answer, and does not assert that mock-site coverage of this boundary exists.
